notes.verdict: Not listed: the profit per trade is smaller than realistic trading costs.
notes.summary: An intraday NIFTY credit spread that is flat by 14:54 every day. It met the goal it was tuned for, a drawdown under 20% with steady years, but it trades almost daily for about 2.6 points a trade. Two points of slippage and charges remove the profit.

costs.name: Skew Afternoon Credit
costs.note: Listed, for comparison · about 1 trade a month

findings: Uses the Momentum Variance signal with a same-day exit, a stop at credit + 40 and one re-entry after a stop.
A profit lock moves the stop to break-even once 20% of the credit is earned; the target is 50% of the credit. This raised average win ÷ average loss from 0.65 to about 1.4.
Lots are capped so one stop loses at most 2.5% of capital, which brought the drawdown from 31% to under 18%.
About 10% of exits had no cached price for the hedge leg. The figures value it from its last trade; booking it at zero gives 16% a year with a 20.2% drawdown.
Tuned on the three years to 30 Sep 2026. The seven weeks after that (1 Oct to 19 Nov 2026, 40 trades) added 10% of capital before costs.

costs.name: Skew Afternoon Credit
costs.note: Listed, for comparison · about 1 trade a month

findings: Rules: 400-point hedge, entries from 10:15, stop near credit + 40, target when the spread is worth 10 or less, everything closed at 14:54.
After a stop it enters once more that day, usually on the other side two minutes later. After a target or a time exit it stops for the day.
Almost all of the profit comes from the first and third years; the second year loses about a third of the capital.
The seven weeks after the three-year study (1 Oct to 19 Nov 2026, 42 trades) added 19% of capital before costs.
